host how Blender Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z, as part of Blender's own undo. Opening a network is an undo step. usdview Edit > Undo / Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z). If the usd-undo plug-in is loaded, it owns those keys and usd_chunks adds none -- two actions on one shortcut make Qt fire neither. Flet, ImGui Not yet.

In usdview a step runs from one user input to the next: a slider drag or a gizmo drag is one undo, and a cook that lands after an edit belongs to that edit's step.

docs.title: For host authors
docs.text: usd_chunks.chunk_undo.History records a stage. A host with its own undo stack stores history.key() with each of its undo steps and calls history.move_to(key) after an undo or redo (see frontends/blender/addon/undo.py). A host without one uses chunk_undo.UndoStack and calls note_input() on each user input (see frontends/qt/undo.py, which does it for any Qt app).

docs.title: Vines: paint, grow, sweep, shade
docs.text:
Ivy on a wall, ready for any renderer. Most renderers, Aurora among them, don't draw curves, so the vine is turned into a mesh and gets a material like any other mesh.

Scatter Brush ──► Vine ──► Curves to Mesh ──► Preview Surface (bark)
                    │
                    └─ Leaf Points ──► Scatter Points (leaf mesh) ──► Preview Surface (leaf)

examples/scripts/ivy_wall.py builds this whole network on a stone wall, with lights and a camera:

USD_CHUNK_DIRS=chunks python examples/scripts/ivy_wall.py

docs.title: The chain
docs.text: Chunk What it does Scatter Brush Paint where the ivy may grow. Wire its Density Field into the Vine's. Vine Grows vines over the paint. Writes a BasisCurves (the stems) and a guide Points cloud (one point per leaf, with the surface normal). Curves to Mesh Sweeps the stems into a tube mesh with UVs, and hides the curves so nothing draws them twice. Preview Surface Binds a bark material to the tube mesh. Scatter Points Instances a leaf mesh on the Vine's Leaf Points. Wire Leaf Points into its Painted Points, and set Up Along Surface to the leaf's tip axis: each leaf then points away from its stem, sized by the Vine.

docs.title: Settings to reach for
docs.text:
• Vine › Growth: Density for how much of the paint gets covered, Meander for how much the stems wind, Climb for how strongly they head up.
  • Vine › Shape: Thickness for stem width, as a share of the painted area.
  • Vine › Leaves: Spacing, Spread (how far leaves sit beside the stem), Bare Base % (no leaves on the oldest part of each stem) and Tip Leaf Size (how small the young leaves at a growing tip are).
  • Vine › Hanging: Hang % sends tendrils off the stem tips. They fall and drape over the mesh.
  • Curves to Mesh › Sides: 6 is plenty at a few metres. Raise it for a close-up.

The roots start at the lowest painted points, but never on a face pointing straight down, such as the buried underside of a wall.

docs.title: Animate it
docs.text:
Turn on Vine › Animation › Animate Growth and set Start and End Frame. The vine grows from nothing to Growth % over those frames. Curves to Mesh sweeps every frame, so the mesh grows too, and Scatter Points shows each leaf from the frame the vine reaches it.

The curves, the mesh and the leaf points all carry a growth primvar: 0 at the roots, 1 at the last tip. A shader can use it to colour young growth, or to grow the vine in at render time instead.

docs.title: Render in Aurora
docs.text:
Export the scene and open it in usdview with Aurora, or render it with usdrecord:

usdrecord --renderer Aurora --camera /World/cam ivy_wall.usda ivy_wall.png

Aurora renders until it has converged, which can take minutes. For a quick look, cap the samples with a RenderSettings prim (int aurora:max_samples = 64) and pass it with --renderSettingsPrimPath.

docs.title: Writing a chunk module
docs.text:
In short: a chunk is a Python module. main() sets up its params, execute(node) does the work, and config() holds details like its description and category.

This page is about writing a new chunk. To make and wire chunks you already have from Python, see Scripting.

A chunk module is a plain .py file. Put it anywhere in a USD_CHUNK_DIRS folder and it's found automatically. You don't need to register it, write a plugInfo.json, or import it anywhere.

A module can define up to four top-level functions. Only main() is required.

Function Required Called main() yes Once per instance, to build a Chunk object. Each node you add to the graph, and each chunk prim loaded from a file, is a separate main() call. config() no Once, when the module is found, for its settings (ChunkConfig). execute(node) no Every time the chunk cooks. See execute(). commit(node) no Once per chunk, after everything has finished cooking. See commit().

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
from usd_chunks import chunk


def main():
    button = chunk.Button("add_cube", "Add Cube")
    button.add_callback(add_cube)

    chunk_api = chunk.Chunk("Add Cubes")
    chunk_api.add_param(button)
    return chunk_api

main() takes no arguments and must return a chunk.Chunk. A Chunk is a Group that also keeps track of its layer, its DAG node and its exec ports. Create its params and groups here, and add their callbacks with add_param and add_callback.

main() runs once per instance, not once when the module is found. Finding the module only imports it and checks that main() exists. After that, main() is called every time a chunk is created: once for each node you add, and once for each saved chunk prim when a file is opened. So anything slow in main(), like building a lookup table, runs again for every node. If that matters, cache it at module level.

Don't change the stage in main(). It runs before the chunk has its prim and its own layer, so anything it writes lands in the wrong place. Anything that changes the stage goes in a callback, in execute(), or in commit().

Callbacks hear their own chunk, never another one. Chunks talk to each other only through wires: an exec input, or an @Node.param@ expression. Both are drawn in the graph and saved in the file. A change in a chunk above yours reaches your chunk as a cook of your execute(), not as a notice. So:

  • add_callback(..., sender=...) takes your own chunk or one of its params. Another chunk's param raises a ValueError.
  • listen_globally=True is for the stage and the host only: stage edits, prim selection, the viewport camera. Listening globally to another chunk's notices (CHUNK_CHANGED, PARAM_CHANGED, ...) raises a ValueError.
  • A param can't depend on another chunk's param through add_dependency. Use connect_value, which writes the expression for you.

A stage listener stays small. When you do listen to the stage or the host:

  • Read the stage and set only your own chunk's params. Never author USD in the callback. execute() authors from the params, so the change reaches the chunks wired below. Camera's Lock to Free Camera works this way: the freecam sets translate and rotate.
  • Write only when the value actually changed. Every write can cook your chunk.
  • Wait for CHUNK_LOADED before writing. Saved values are restored after main(), and a write before then can overwrite them.
  • Return early on rounds that can't matter to you. A stage listener runs on every stage change, for every instance of your chunk.

Most of the time you don't need a listener at all. A menu of what's on the stage (the cameras, a prim's variant sets, the SkelRoots) is only needed when someone opens it. Give your module a menu_items hook instead, and every frontend asks it as the menu opens:

def menu_items(node, param_name):
    if param_name == "camera":
        return [str(p.GetPath()) for p in node.get_stage().Traverse() if p.IsA(UsdGeom.Camera)]
    return None   # this menu keeps its items

The current value always stays listed, so a saved pick survives until the stage offers it.

A chunk that follows the host application's own scene (Blender's objects, say) defines host_changed(node). The host calls it, debounced, after the user edits the scene; the module decides whether what it reads moved and calls node.execute() if so. Blender's add-on calls it today; see chunks/modelling/blender_import.py.

docs/example.md has a longer example with notes on the param types, groups, flags and callback signatures you can use in main().

docs.title: Icons in the node graph
docs.text:
A node shows an icon in its header, and a group can show one beside its name. Only the chunk decides them; nothing else picks one, so a chunk or group that sets no icon shows none.

The node's icon goes in config(), so every node of the chunk gets it:

def config():
    return chunk.DefaultConfig(
        category=chunk.StandardCategory.MODELLING,
        icon="posts",
    )

A group's icon goes on the group, in main():

run_grp = chunk.Group("Run", icon="ruler", flags=_GF)

icon takes either:

  • the name of a built-in icon: a file name, without .svg, from usd_chunks/resources/icons/node/ (sun, move, rotate, cube, camera, eye, ...). Built-in icons are drawn in one colour, and each has a default colour.
  • a path to your own image file (.svg or .png), drawn as it is.

On a group or a param, anything else raises a ValueError.

Which icon a node shows, first match wins:

  1. The icon on the chunk's prim in USD (see below), for that one node.
  2. icon set on the chunk in main() (chunk_api.icon = "sun"), for every node of it.
  3. icon in config().

Per node, in USD. A node's icon and colour can also be set on its chunk prim, through USD's own UsdUINodeGraphNodeAPI. These are saved in the file, and the node updates as soon as they change:

from pxr import Gf, Sdf, UsdUI

api = UsdUI.NodeGraphNodeAPI.Apply(chunk_prim)
api.CreateIconAttr().Set(Sdf.AssetPath("camera"))          # a built-in name or an image path
api.CreateDisplayColorAttr().Set(Gf.Vec3f(1.0, 0.4, 0.3))  # the icon's colour

The lookup is usd_chunks/chunk_icons.py, so any graph frontend can show the same icons.

docs.title: config()
docs.text:
from usd_chunks import chunk


def config():
    return chunk.DefaultConfig(
        category=chunk.StandardCategory.MODELLING,
        description="""
        Resets a prim's transform: clears every authored transform op.

        Writes an empty xformOpOrder on the prim, so none of its transform ops apply.
        """,
    )

The description opens with one summary line, then a blank line, then the details. The summary line says what jobs the chunk does, in the words someone asking for them would use, in at most 90 characters, without repeating the chunk's name. It sums up the text below it, so it claims nothing that text doesn't say. usdchunks list and the create menu's search show only that line, so it decides whether a person or an agent finds the chunk at all.

config() returns a chunk.DefaultConfig, a small subclass of chunk_core.ChunkConfig. It describes how the chunk is loaded and how it shows up in menus. A module without config() gets the defaults below.

Field Default Meaning category "Chunks" Where the chunk appears in the create menu. Use a StandardCategory member (MODELLING, DYNAMICS, TRANSFORM, UTILS, RIGS, USER, EXAMPLES, USD, PROPERTIES, USD_RENDER, USD_LAYER, CORE, MATERIALS, MTLX) or a plain string for your own. description "Chunk description..." Shown in tooltips and the create menu. ChunkGroup's doc param uses the same text to describe what a saved network does, for a person or an AI reading the file. load_for_plugin None Only load the chunk in one host plugin (e.g. "chunk_usdview"), if it only works there. hosts [] The applications the chunk runs in, each a name with an optional minimum version: ["houdini>=21.5", "blender>=5.1"]. Empty or not set: every host. Elsewhere the chunk is skipped. Import a host-only module (bpy, hou) under try/except ImportError, so other hosts can still read config(). requirements [] pip packages the module needs, e.g. ["numpy>=2,<3"]. If one is missing and the module fails to import, it's skipped instead of crashing. usdview and usdchunks run ask whether to install the missing ones into USD_CHUNK_DEPENDENCY_DIR (see USD_CHUNK_AUTO_INSTALL). required_modules [] Other chunk modules that must be loaded for this one to work. interactive False The chunk writes to a file layer that is kept, instead of its own layer being rebuilt on every cook. Use it for a chunk that makes a one-off edit rather than something that is re-cooked. cache_cook False Keep this chunk's cooked result on disk and read it back instead of cooking again, when nothing it depends on has changed. For a slow cook whose result depends only on its params, the files they name and the stage's units. See Caching a slow cook. cache_always False cache_cook that can't be turned off: no Cache Result checkbox, USD_CHUNKS_COOK_CACHE=0 doesn't apply, and quick cooks are stored too. For a result that is expensive or impossible to remake anywhere else, such as Blender Import's. cook_on_open False Cook this chunk every time a network opens, instead of reading back the result kept when it was saved. For a result that depends on something no key can see: the clock, an unseeded random, a web request. See Opening without cooking. hidden False Left out of the create menu. For a type that is only saved and loaded, never created by hand, like runtime, the type a chunk built in Python is saved as (see Building a chunk at runtime). It still has to be a registered module, because that's how loading a file knows what to rebuild. terminal False The chunk has no outputs:chunk, so it ends an exec chain. The View and Output chunks use this. exec_inputs 1 How many numbered exec input ports the chunk has. 1 is the normal case: one inputs:chunk port, which can still take several wires. With more than 1, each slot gets its own port and it matters which wire goes where. For example, Stage Expression Switch has a normal path on slot 0 and a matched path on slot 1, and only one of them runs. dynamic_exec_inputs False The chunk adds a new numbered exec input port for each wire connected to it, plus one empty port for the next one. For chunks like Merge or Switch, where each incoming branch needs its own port. Unlike exec_inputs, the number of ports isn't fixed. outputs [] Extra typed output ports beyond outputs:chunk, as [(name, SdfTypeName), ...]. variants [] Extra entries in the chunk's submenu in the create menu, as [(label, {param: value}), ...], or a function that returns that list. Use a function when the list is slow to build (for example, listing a shader registry). It then only runs the first time the menu is shown, not every time chunks are loaded. gizmos [] Viewport handles that control this chunk's params. See Chunk gizmos: the host contract.

Keep config() self-contained. When the module is found, config() is run on its own, with only the module's usd_chunks imports done. This way, reading a module's config never runs the rest of its code. If config() uses a constant or helper from the module, the first try fails with NameError. The registry then tries once more after running the module's top-level assignments and defs. If any of those need a non-usd_chunks import, that fails too, and the module falls back to the DefaultConfig() defaults: wrong category, generic description, and only a warning in the log. If config() needs something slow to build, pass a function to variants (see the table above) instead of a constant built in the module.

docs.title: execute()
docs.text:
def execute(node: chunk.Chunk) -> None:
    ...

execute is a reserved name at module level. Don't use it for a normal callback, or it will be called every time the chunk cooks.

If a module has execute(node), it runs every time the chunk cooks: when something it depends on changes (add_dependency), when the chunk is loaded from a file, or when the exec chain is run again. On load, param values are restored, but callbacks don't run again (see below). node is the chunk itself, the same object main() returned. So execute usually calls node.get_stage() or node.get_edit_context() and then changes the stage.

It runs with a Usd.EditContext already set to the chunk's own layer (unless the chunk is interactive, which writes somewhere else). Every execute() starts from an empty layer, so write the whole result every time. It must give the same result every time it runs with the same inputs, in the same order: a prim written in dict or set order moves about. It can run many times while the graph cooks, so keep it fast.

The framework then changes the chunk's layer only where the result differs (a diff cook): a prim that comes out the same sends no change, and a changed value is set in place, so the viewport updates it rather than building it again. For that, the cook runs on a stage of the layers upstream of the chunk, writing into a scratch layer. Read and write through node.get_stage() and node.get_edit_context(), never the scene's stage (node.get_scene_stage()), which doesn't hold that layer; keep the scene's stage for the scene's own bookkeeping, such as wiring chunk prims. Key anything kept between cooks on node.get_layer_identifier(), not the edit layer's identifier. A chunk that changes the layer stack or what is muted, or sublayers its own layer, is cleared and rewritten instead. USD_CHUNKS_DIFF_COOK=0 turns diff cooks off.

You write execute(node); you don't call it directly. To run a chunk again, call chunk.execute(): it re-executes the chunk and everything that depends on it, the same as when a param changes. Changing a param or a wire already does this, so a module only needs it when its result is out of date in a way no param change says -- say, it restored params its first cook could not see.

An execute that sets many params -- a Wedge writing a variant's ranges -- sets them inside with chunk.change_block():. Then what they drive cooks once, after the last one, rather than once per value.

A common pattern is a chunk that does its real work in a param callback, with execute only there to redo that work after the file is opened. This is why execute exists, instead of doing everything in callbacks:

def _run(owner, notice, sender):
    ...
    UsdGeom.Xformable(prim).ClearXformOpOrder()


def execute(node: chunk.Chunk) -> None:
    """load_chunks calls this once per chunk after bulk-restoring its param values, so a
    reloaded chunk actually redoes its work — the real logic lives in _run, a Button
    callback, which load's value-restore deliberately does not trigger."""
    _run(node, None, None)


def main():
    chunk_api = chunk.Chunk("Reset Transform")
    ...
    run_btn.add_callback(_run)
    return chunk_api

(the full version is chunks/transforms/reset_transform.py). A save only stores a chunk's data (params, values and wiring), never the code that ran (see What a save keeps). execute is what makes a chunk do its work again after the file is opened.

docs.title: Caching a slow cook
docs.text:
Before caching a slow cook, check whether it needs to be slow. Authoring thousands of prims through the Usd API, or looping over points in Python, is usually 10× or more slower than it has to be. See Making a chunk fast.

Because a cook with the same inputs always gives the same layer, a slow one doesn't have to run again. Set cache_cook=True in config() and the result is kept on disk and read back the next time the inputs match, including after the file is closed and opened again:

def config():
    return chunk.DefaultConfig(cache_cook=True)

The cache compares everything it can see:

  • every param's value (an expression counts as the value it resolves to), except labels and OUTPUT params, which the cook writes;
  • the size and modification time of any file a param names;
  • the module's own code and the files next to it;
  • the stage's up axis and metersPerUnit.

If the result also depends on something that is not a param, for example geometry read from an upstream chunk or files named inside another file, add a cache_key(node) function that returns it. Anything that can be repr()ed works. Return None when it can't be worked out, and the chunk cooks as usual:

def cache_key(node):
    return [mesh_checksum(prim) for prim in input_meshes(node)]

Poly Reduce returns a checksum of the meshes it reads, and URDF Import returns the size and date of each mesh file the .urdf names.

Some results are not made in a cook: a simulation bakes when you press Run, on a worker thread. To cache one, take the entry when the work starts and store the layer when it is done. The next cook with the same inputs reads it back, also after the file is opened again. Taking the entry first means a param changed during the bake does not relabel it:

def cache_key(node):
    return sim_bake.input_key(node)  # None in ordinary cooks: no automatic caching

entry = sim_bake.cache_entry(node, sim_bake.digest(job))  # None when caching is off
if entry is not None and entry.restore(node, layer):
    ...                               # read back: no bake
...                                   # else bake into the chunk's layer, then
if entry is not None:
    entry.store(node, layer)

cache_key answers only while cache_entry asks, because working out a bake's inputs can take seconds, too slow for every cook. The RBD Solver and the Particle Solver do this.

Each chunk of such a module gets a Cache Result checkbox, on by default, to switch caching off for that one node. Only cooks that take longer than about 50 ms are stored, since reading a result back takes time too. A cook that changes its own input params, or adds params, is never stored. For where the cache lives and how to switch it off, see USD_CHUNKS_COOK_CACHE.

docs.title: Opening without cooking
docs.text:
A saved network holds the chunks and their wires, not their results. So when you save, each chunk's layer is also kept in the cook cache, and when the network is opened again, each chunk reads its layer back instead of cooking, as long as nothing it depends on has changed. This is for every chunk; cache_cook is not needed.

A chunk's result is read back only if all of these are the same as when it was saved:

  • everything cache_cook compares (its params, the files they name, its module's code, the stage's units);
  • its exec wires and what the framework keeps on its chunk prim;
  • the same for every chunk upstream of it;
  • the network file's own prims and time range, and the size and date of the files it sublayers or references.

Otherwise it cooks, as it always did. A chunk whose last cook also wrote outside its own layer (into the session layer, like a MaterialX Shader's input wires) or changed the layer stack always cooks. So does a module that sets cook_on_open=True.

To switch it off, set USD_CHUNKS_OPEN_CACHE=0.

docs.title: Long bakes: sim_bake
docs.text:
A simulation that takes seconds or minutes must not stop the host. Write the bake as a generator and hand it to sim_bake.run. Read the scene first, then yield sim_bake.WORKER: what follows runs on a worker thread, so it must not touch USD. yield sim_bake.MAIN comes back to the main thread to write the result:

from usd_chunks import sim_bake

def bake(ctx):
    job = read_inputs(stage)          # main thread
    yield sim_bake.WORKER
    result = solve(job, progress=ctx.progress, cancelled=ctx.cancelled)
    yield sim_bake.MAIN
    write_result(stage, result)       # main thread
    return result

sim_bake.run(node, bake, report=show_in_readout, finish=when_done)

Headless and under test there is no event loop to come back to, so the bake runs straight through. sim_bake.cancel(node) stops it.

Some engines hold Python's GIL while they compute (Taichi does), which stops the UI even from a thread. Call the solve through sim_bake.in_subprocess(ctx, solve, **job) to run it in a separate Python process. promote, keep and restore handle the bake's layer: put it in front of the layers it animates, and put it back after the next cook rewrites it.

For smaller work of your own -- a download, a wait before re-running -- get back to the main thread with node.get_scene().call_later(fn, delay=0.0). It works in every host (usdview, Blender) and from any thread, and returns a function that cancels the call, which is all a debounce needs:

def _schedule(node):
    cancel = getattr(node, "_pending", None)
    if cancel:
        cancel()                      # a newer change: the last wait no longer counts
    node._pending = node.get_scene().call_later(lambda: rerun(node), delay=0.6)

Don't import Qt for this. A chunk that imports PySide6 doesn't load in a host without it.

docs.title: Skipping cooks nothing reached
docs.text:
A change to a chunk dirties everything below it, but most of those chunks read nothing that changed: a Scatter below a Light doesn't care that the Light turned. So a chunk that only the chunks above it changed doesn't cook unless one of them changed a prim it reads.

What a chunk reads is not declared anywhere. During a cook, node.get_stage() returns a stage that only holds the chunk's inputs (the prims its prim path params name, such as PRIM_SELECTION params and primpath_location) and the prims its last cook wrote. So:

  • Read the prims you need through a prim path param, not a path written into the code. A chunk that looks up anything else, or walks the whole stage (Traverse()), is noticed, cooked again on the whole stage, and never skipped from then on. It still works; it just always cooks.
  • Framework work on the scene, like muting a gate's branches, goes through node.get_scene_stage(), which is always the whole scene. Module code shouldn't need it.

Anything the framework can't account for makes the chunks below cook, as they always have: a rewire, a chunk disabled above, a change to which layers are muted or to the stage's expression variables, an Edit Target repointed.

docs.title: commit()
docs.text:
def commit(node: chunk.Chunk) -> None:
    ...

commit is for a chunk whose job is writing a file, not writing to its own USD layer, for example Export USD or a render product chunk. It's separate from execute because they run at different times:

  • execute runs many times while the graph cooks and params change. It's the right place for fast USD edits, and the wrong place for writing to disk.
  • commit runs once, after everything has finished cooking. usdchunks run calls it, and so does Scene.commit() from Python. usdview doesn't call it on its own; a chunk like Export USD has a button for that. Chunks commit in graph order, so a chunk that reads another chunk's output sees the finished result.

No edit context is set up for commit. It reads the final composed stage and writes to disk. Modules without commit are skipped, since most chunks have nothing to write. A disabled chunk, or one that isn't connected to the active view, never commits.

docs.title: Lofting params a module builds at runtime
docs.text:
Lofting publishes a param's saved attribute on its group. A param flagged TRANSIENT has none: it's session state, rebuilt rather than saved. A module whose transient params should still be loftable (Property Editor's fields are) defines these:

def promote_param(node, param):
    """Return a saved param to loft in place of the transient `param`, or None."""

def restore_params(node, prim):
    """On load, before saved values are read back: build the promoted params again."""

def param_unlofted(node, param):
    """`param` was just unlofted from its group."""

promote_param runs when a transient param is lofted, and the group publishes the param it returns. That param isn't in what main() builds, so on load restore_params builds it again from the chunk's prim, before its value and its link to the group are restored. Property Editor keeps the list of promoted attributes in a hidden saved param for this.

docs.title: Discovery, recap
docs.text:
Every folder in USD_CHUNK_DIRS, including subfolders, is searched for .py files. Any file with a top-level main() is registered under its file name. There are no other rules for folder layout or file names. Environment variables explains which one wins when two folders have a chunk with the same name.

To check what was found, run usdchunks list (or usdchunks list <word>). usdchunks show <name> prints a chunk as someone looking for one sees it: its description, its menu entries and every param, with its type, default and range.

docs.title: usd_chunks
docs.text:
usd_chunks: interactive UI panels ("chunks") for OpenUSD, built from plain Python modules.

Importing the package checks that the OpenUSD bindings are importable, sets the usd_chunks logger's level (from USD_CHUNK_LOG_LEVEL), and checks the attrs version. It adds no console handler; entry points call configure_logging() for that.

docs.text:

Send usd_chunks log records to the console, unless the host already logs somewhere.

Called by the entry points, not on import. Idempotent. Skipped when the root logger has a handler: records propagate there, and a second handler would print each one twice.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default level int

The least severe record printed. A script Scene prints warnings and up.

DEBUG Source code in usd_chunks/__init__.py 
def configure_logging(level: int = logging.DEBUG) -> None:
    """Send ``usd_chunks`` log records to the console, unless the host already logs somewhere.

    Called by the entry points, not on import. Idempotent. Skipped when the root logger has a
    handler: records propagate there, and a second handler would print each one twice.

    Args:
        level: The least severe record printed. A script Scene prints warnings and up.
    """
    global _console_handler
    if _console_handler is not None or logging.getLogger().handlers:
        return
    _console_handler = logging.StreamHandler()
    _console_handler.setLevel(level)
    _console_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter(
        "%(levelname)s: %(asctime)s - %(name)s: %(message)s", datefmt="%y-%m-%d %H:%M"
    ))
    _logger.addHandler(_console_handler)

docs.title: usd_chunks.chunk
docs.text:
The client-facing chunk API: the concrete chunk, group and param classes.

These classes can be used by themselves, but they also describe common UI information, which makes them easy to implement in any UI framework.

As all chunk classes use chunk_core.AttributesMetaclass, they are all attrs classes (dataclasses). Creating a new param class only takes declaring the class and inheriting from ChunkParamBase or a related base class. The class is wrapped in attrs.define() behind the scenes, so it gets some methods for free, most notably __init__(), built from all the fields of the class, inherited ones included. For this reason, any attribute of a chunk class should be declared with attrs.field().

A class inheriting from ChunkParamBase needs to implement get_type, and evaluate_type too if the type can change at runtime. That is what maps a param to a widget in whatever UI framework is used.

Example

class CustomStrParam(ChunkParamBase[str]):
    some_attrib: str = attrs.field(default="hello")

    @classmethod
    def get_type(cls) -> ChunkFlags.ParamType:
        return ChunkFlags.ParamType.LINEEDIT

In a chunk module, chunk.Chunk() is the top-level container that every param and group is added to. A chunk with a button is as simple as:

Example

from usd_chunks import chunk


def main():
    my_chunk = chunk.Chunk("my_chunk")
    button = chunk.Button("my_button")

    my_chunk.add_param(button)
    return my_chunk

See example for a more extensive example.

@classmethod
def from_usd_rel(cls, rel: Usd.Relationship, *args, **kwargs):
    """Create a param that holds a relationship's targets as paths.

    Args:
        rel: The relationship.
        *args: Passed to the param constructor.
        **kwargs: Passed to the param constructor; `name` defaults to the relationship's
            base name.

    Returns:
        The new param.
    """
    rel_name = rel.GetName()

    if (args and isinstance(args[0], str)) or kwargs.get("name"):
        param = cls(*args, **kwargs)
    else:
        kwargs["name"] = rel_name.split(":")[-1]
        param = cls(*args, **kwargs)
    try:
        if sender := param.get_attribute_sender("value"):
            param.set_usd_prop(str(rel.GetPath()), sender)
    except AttributeError:
        pass
    return param

def resolve_paths(self) -> list[str]:

docs.text:
refresh_items()

Ask the chunk's module for this menu's items, as the menu is about to open.

A menu of what is on the stage -- the SkelRoots a Skel Pose can pose -- is wanted only when someone looks at it. A chunk opts in with a module-level function::

def menu_items(node, param_name):
    return _skel_roots(node.get_stage()) if param_name == "primpath_location" else None

so it need not listen to the stage to keep a list current that nobody opens, and need not cook to fill it either: a cook is skipped when nothing it reads changed, and a stage walk would be a read of everything. A frontend calls this before it shows the list; None from the hook leaves the items as they are.

A Menu lofted onto a chunkgroup refreshes the inner Menu it stands for, whose items it mirrors (chunk_stage._mirror_menu_items).

Source code in usd_chunks/chunk.py 
def refresh_items(self) -> None:
    """Ask the chunk's module for this menu's items, as the menu is about to open.

    A menu of what is on the stage -- the SkelRoots a Skel Pose can pose -- is wanted
    only when someone looks at it. A chunk opts in with a module-level function::

        def menu_items(node, param_name):
            return _skel_roots(node.get_stage()) if param_name == "primpath_location" else None

    so it need not listen to the stage to keep a list current that nobody opens, and
    need not cook to fill it either: a cook is skipped when nothing it reads changed,
    and a stage walk would be a read of everything. A frontend calls this before it
    shows the list; None from the hook leaves the items as they are.

    A Menu lofted onto a chunkgroup refreshes the inner Menu it stands for, whose items
    it mirrors (chunk_stage._mirror_menu_items).
    """
    inner = getattr(self, "_loft_inner_menu", None)
    if inner is not None:
        if (inner_menu := inner()) is not None:
            inner_menu.refresh_items()
        return
    node = self.get_chunk()
    hook = node._module_hook(MENU_ITEMS_HOOK) if node is not None else None
    if hook is None:
        return
    try:
        items = hook(node, self.name)
    except Exception:
        # A failing hook leaves the list as it was: a stale list beats an empty one.
        logger.exception("menu_items hook failed for %r on chunk %r", self.name, node.name)
        return
    if items is not None:
        self.set_items(items)

def set_items(self, items) -> None:
    """Replace menu_items with items, keeping the current value listed.

    The current value stays in the list even when items no longer has it: a saved
    choice arrives before the upstream chunk that makes it has cooked, and a view-driven
    recook mutes layers one at a time, so "not there right now" is routinely transient.
    Dropping it would lose the choice for good.

    Only assigned when something changed: menu_items is a plain field, and writing it
    re-triggers the chunk's execute() whether or not anything differs.

    Args:
        items: The new choices.
    """
    current = self.value or ""
    items = list(items)
    if current and current not in items and not chunk_utils.has_expression(current):
        items.append(current)
    if list(self.menu_items or []) != items:
        self.menu_items = items

def anchor_file(node, path: str) -> str:
    """path as a chunk should author it, for USD to resolve: a ./ or ../ path anchored to
    the network's folder.

    In a USD file such a path is relative to that file. A param's value is saved in the
    network file, but a chunk authors it into its own anonymous layer, which would anchor
    it to the working directory instead. A search path (no ./ or ../) is left as it is: the
    stage's resolver looks for it in the network's folder already.

    Args:
        node: The chunk, for its stage.
        path: The param's value.
    """
    stage = node.get_stage() if hasattr(node, "get_stage") else None
    return asset_paths.anchor(path, stage)

docs.title: change_block
docs.text:
change_block()

Make every value set inside the block one change: what it affects cooks once, at the end.

Each value set outside a block cooks everything below it straight away. Setting several cooks them several times, each time against a half-new set of values::

mc = scene.create.mychunk()
with chunk.change_block():
    mc.get_param("param1").value = 1
    mc.get_param("param2").value = 2
# mychunk, and everything below it, cooked once, with both values

Inside the block a value change only marks what it affects; callbacks run, and chunks cook, when the block ends. Blocks nest: an inner one joins the outermost. For a script, and for a module whose execute() sets many params of its own (a Wedge writing a variant's ranges).

The same for a script building a network. Made outside a block, each chunk wired below the last cooks the whole chain above it again: a 336-chunk network took 17-27 minutes to build. Inside one, each chunk a script makes (scene.create) cooks once as it is made, before it is wired -- a Light builds its params in its cook, for the script to set next, and a Layer chunk makes its layer for an Edit Target made after it -- and what changed cooks once at the end, upstream first: about two cooks a chunk in all. Readouts read inside the block are from that first, unwired cook.

Chunks created inside the block are placed in the stage's layer stack when it ends, once their wiring is known (ChunkLayerManager.defer_placement), rather than each one as a graph of its own first and moved when wired. Once it has cooked, the layers are ranked as the next chunk made would rank them, and the stage is looked over once for chunk prims that arrived by USD (chunk_cook.after_batch).

@contextmanager
def change_block() -> Iterator[None]:
    """Make every value set inside the block one change: what it affects cooks once, at the end.

    Each value set outside a block cooks everything below it straight away. Setting several
    cooks them several times, each time against a half-new set of values::

        mc = scene.create.mychunk()
        with chunk.change_block():
            mc.get_param("param1").value = 1
            mc.get_param("param2").value = 2
        # mychunk, and everything below it, cooked once, with both values

    Inside the block a value change only marks what it affects; callbacks run, and chunks
    cook, when the block ends. Blocks nest: an inner one joins the outermost. For a script,
    and for a module whose execute() sets many params of its own (a Wedge writing a
    variant's ranges).

    The same for a script building a network. Made outside a block, each chunk wired below
    the last cooks the whole chain above it again: a 336-chunk network took 17-27 minutes to
    build. Inside one, each chunk a script makes (scene.create) cooks once as it is made,
    before it is wired -- a Light builds its params in its cook, for the script to set next,
    and a Layer chunk makes its layer for an Edit Target made after it -- and what changed
    cooks once at the end, upstream first: about two cooks a chunk in all. Readouts read
    inside the block are from that first, unwired cook.

    Chunks created inside the block are placed in the stage's layer stack when it ends,
    once their wiring is known (ChunkLayerManager.defer_placement), rather than each one
    as a graph of its own first and moved when wired. Once it has cooked, the layers are
    ranked as the next chunk made would rank them, and the stage is looked over once for
    chunk prims that arrived by USD (chunk_cook.after_batch).
    """
    with chunk_cook.batched_solve():
        lm = ChunkLayerManager()
        placing = lm.initialized and lm.defer_placement()
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            # Before the solve the block ends with: a cook needs its layer on the stage.
            if placing:
                lm.place_deferred_layers()

def create_chunks(module_name: str, anonymous=False) -> Sequence[Chunk]:
    """Find a ChunkModule in the registry and run it's main() function, then add the resulting chunk(s) to the scene if not anonymous.

    To build a network from a script, use `scene.create.<module>(...)` instead (see
    docs/scripting.md): it also sets params, wires chunks together and reaches menu
    variants. This stays for making a chunk without adding it (anonymous=True).

    Args:
        module_name (str): The name of the module to load, relative to USD_CHUNK_DIRS
        anonymous (bool, optional): If set to True, the resulting chunks will be added to the scene directly. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Sequence[Chunk]: The created chunks
    """
    if not (reg := get_chunk_registry()):
        return []

    if not (mod := reg.get_chunk_module(module_name)):
        return []

    if not mod.loaded:
        chunks = mod.load()
    else:
        chunks = mod.create()

    chunks = cast(list[Chunk], chunks)

    if not anonymous:
        for c in chunks:
            reg.scene.add_chunk(c)

    return chunks

def is_param_t(t: ChunkFlags.ParamType | type[ValueT]) -> Predicate[ChunkParamBase] | Predicate[ChunkParamBase[ValueT]]:
    """Create a predicate matching params of a value type or a ParamType.

    A value type matches a param holding a value of that type; a ChunkFlags.ParamType
    matches a param whose evaluate_type() includes it.

    Args:
        t (ChunkFlags.ParamType | type): The value type or ParamType to match

    Returns:
        Predicate[ChunkParamBase]: The predicate function
    """
    if isinstance(t, ChunkFlags.ParamType):

        def _fn_e(v) -> TypeGuard[ChunkParamBase]:
            if not is_param(v):
                return False
            return t in v.evaluate_type()

        return _fn_e

    def _fn_t(v) -> TypeGuard[ChunkParamBase]:
        if not is_param(v):
            return False
        return t in ChunkFlags.ParamTypeToTypes(v.evaluate_type())

    return _fn_t

def param_from_attr(attr: Usd.Attribute, *args, **kwargs) -> ChunkCommon | None:
    """Create a param for a Usd.Attribute, if its type is supported.

    Uses the from_usd_attr class method of the matching param type, which connects the
    ATTRIBUTE_CHANGED notice so the param controls the USD attribute. The result is a
    ChunkCommon rather than a ChunkParamBase because some params are really groups
    (Vectors, for example).

    Args:
        attr (Usd.Attribute): The attribute to create a param for
        *args: Passed to the param constructor.
        **kwargs: Passed to the param constructor.

    Returns:
        ChunkCommon | None: The param, or None if no param type maps the attr's type.
    """
    type_name = attr.GetTypeName()

    t = usd_type_map.get(str(type_name))
    if not t:
        return None
    if isinstance(t, tuple):
        kwargs.update(t[1])
        return t[0].from_usd_attr(attr, *args, **kwargs)
    else:
        return t.from_usd_attr(attr, *args, **kwargs)

def resolve_file(node, path: str) -> str:
    """The file a param's path names, found as USD would find it; "" if there is none.

    For a chunk that opens its file itself (a CAD or URDF import) rather than handing the
    path to USD. A relative path is a search path from the network's folder, so the chunk
    reads the same file whatever the working directory, as a Sublayer or Reference does.

    Args:
        node: The chunk, for its stage's resolver context.
        path: The param's value.
    """
    path = (path or "").strip()
    if not path:
        return ""
    stage = node.get_stage() if hasattr(node, "get_stage") else None
    return asset_paths.resolve(path, stage)

def show_attribute(prim, target_group, collapse_non_inputs=True, var_selections=None):
    """Populate a group with typed editable params for all attributes and relationships on a prim.

    This is the shared utility for dynamically building attribute editor UIs.
    Used by the Dynamic chunk, Light chunk, and any chunk that needs to expose
    a prim's attributes as interactive widgets.

    Args:
        prim: The Usd.Prim whose attributes to display.
        target_group: A ChunkGroupBase to populate with params. Existing children
            are cleared before populating -- unless this group was last populated from
            the same attributes, in which case they are kept and re-authored.
        collapse_non_inputs: If True, namespace groups other than 'inputs' start
            collapsed. Keeps the UI tidy for prims with many attributes.
        var_selections: The (anchor_prim_path, vs_name, variant) tuples active when `prim`
            was resolved (split_variant_path / author_in_variant_context), if any. Recorded
            on each generated attribute param so a later edit re-enters the same variant
            (author_in_variant_selections) instead of authoring outside it -- see
            ChunkUsdAttributeSupport.data_changed. None, the default, takes whichever
            variant scopes are open around `prim` right now
            (chunk_utils.open_variant_selections), so a call inside
            author_in_variant_contexts' loop records its variant without being told. Pass
            () to record none.
    """
    if not prim or not prim.IsValid():
        # Clean existing params: no prim means nothing to show.
        for grp in target_group.get_my_params():
            grp.request_delete()
        target_group._shown_signature = None
        return

    if var_selections is None:
        var_selections = chunk_utils.open_variant_selections(prim.GetStage(), prim.GetPath())

    # The same attributes as last time, and every param still bound: keep the params.
    #
    # A chunk that shows its own prim (Light) calls this on every cook, and every edit to
    # one of these params is a cook -- rebuilding here deleted and recreated every param and
    # its widget on each tick of a slider, the one being dragged included. A param binds to
    # its attribute by path, so an unchanged signature means each existing param is already
    # bound to the right place. What the cook's cleared layer lost is only what they
    # authored -- the driven connection and value of a param that was edited -- and the
    # framework authors those again after the cook (ChunkBase.reauthor_driven_attrs). An
    # untouched param authors nothing and reads the schema fallback, the same as before.
    try:
        signature = _shown_signature(prim, var_selections, collapse_non_inputs)
    except RuntimeError:
        logger.debug("show_attribute: %s went away while it was being read; leaving this "
                     "chunk's params alone for the next cook", prim.GetPath())
        return
    if (signature == getattr(target_group, "_shown_signature", None)
            and target_group.get_my_params()
            and _shown_params_bound(target_group, str(prim.GetPath()))):
        return

    # Read the prim FIRST, and build every param, before touching target_group at all.
    #
    # Installing a param fires notices; a cook reached that way can recompose the stage; and
    # a resync EXPIRES this prim handle along with every attribute already read off it, so
    # the next read raises. For example, a Stage Expression Switch writes the record of
    # what it muted, that write cascades into cooking a light on the branch it just
    # suppressed, and the light's own prim is gone by the time this loop reaches its
    # second attribute.
    #
    # Raising there is not a local failure -- the exception would escape into
    # gate_to_branches and leave the gate half done, with the branch it was suppressing
    # still composed. Collecting first turns that into a lost cook rather than a
    # half-emptied chunk: nothing has been deleted yet, the params the chunk already has
    # stay exactly as they were, and the next cook rebuilds them.
    prim_path = prim.GetPath()
    specs = []
    try:
        for attr in prim.GetAttributes():
            specs.append((attr.GetNamespace(),
                          param_from_attr(attr, var_selections=var_selections),
                          collapse_non_inputs))
        for rel in prim.GetRelationships():
            specs.append((rel.GetNamespace(), param_from_rel(rel), False))
    except RuntimeError:
        logger.debug("show_attribute: %s went away while it was being read; leaving this "
                     "chunk's params alone for the next cook", prim_path)
        return

    # Clean existing params, now that there is something to replace them with.
    for grp in target_group.get_my_params():
        grp.request_delete()

    groups = {}
    for ns, param, collapse in specs:
        if not param:
            continue

        if not isinstance(param, ChunkGroupBase):
            param.set_flag(ChunkFlags.ParamFlags.LABELED)

        tgt_grp = target_group if not ns else groups.get(ns)
        if not tgt_grp:
            tgt_grp = Group(
                ns,
                flags=ChunkFlags.GroupFlags.COLLAPSABLE | ChunkFlags.GroupFlags.LABELED,
            )
            if collapse and ns and ns != "inputs":
                tgt_grp.set_state(ChunkFlags.State.COLLAPSED)
            target_group.add_param(tgt_grp)
            groups[ns] = tgt_grp

        tgt_grp.add_param(param)

    target_group._shown_signature = signature

docs.title: usd_chunks.chunk_core
docs.text:
The base classes every chunk object derives from.

These classes are not meant to be instantiated; use the implementations in usd_chunks.chunk.

The attrs library gives every chunk class dataclass-like attributes. The attributes and methods attrs generates are inherited through the MRO, so a subclass only declares its fields and attrs builds init and the rest. Instead of @attrs.define, every chunk object uses AttributesMetaclass, which wraps each class in attrs.define with the right settings and adds custom validation and conversion.

All chunk objects inherit from ChunkCommon, which declares the fields every chunk object has, such as name. Every field that can change has an AttributeSender, and since AttributeSender is a ChunkNoticePropagator, attribute changes propagate up the hierarchy and send notices.

def get_chunk_module(self) -> chunk_registry.ChunkModule | None:
    """The registered module this chunk's type names, or None.

    Looked up in the registry by config.module -- the same name a saved file records as
    info:chunkType -- rather than held on the chunk. A chunk can therefore only ever run
    what a registered module defines, which is exactly what reopening the file will run:
    a saved file is the whole description of what the network does.

    The registry's module is the copy chunks are built from. A chunk module can exist
    twice in sys.modules under different keys (its bare name, and a package path when
    its folder is importable), so it is found by the registry's name, never by import.

    A dict lookup (ChunkRegistry.get_chunk_module does no discovery), so it is cheap
    enough for the gizmo hooks, which are asked per draw and per drag tick.

    Returns:
        The ChunkModule, or None for a chunk no module made (a plain Chunk built in the
        interpreter, a tab context) or whose module is not registered.
    """
    if not (cfg := self._config) or not cfg.module:
        return None
    return chunk_registry.ChunkRegistry().get_chunk_module(cfg.module)

def reauthor_driven_attrs(self) -> None:
    """Author again the connection and value of every param of this chunk that drives a
    real prim attribute (connect_usd_attr).

    Those live in the chunk's layer, but they are the params' state rather than what a
    cook produced: a param is bound once -- by the module, by show_attribute, or on
    being edited away from its default -- and stays bound whether or not the next cook
    binds it again. The framework clears the layer before every cook, so it puts them
    back after one. Only this chunk's own params: a chunk nested inside keeps its own.
    """
    for _, param in self.iter_hierarchy():
        if getattr(param, "_driven_attr_paths", None) and param.get_chunk() is self:
            param._author_driven_connections()

def trigger_on_create_callbacks(self, notice=None, sender=None):
    """Trigger every on-create callback in this chunk's hierarchy.

    Runs once the chunk is loaded and added to the scene, as a callback on CHUNK_LOADED.
    Outside the chunk's edit context: each callback triggered runs in its own owner's.

    Args:

        sender: The sender, when called as a callback.

    for _, child in self.iter_hierarchy():
        for cb in child.get_on_create_callbacks():
            if cb.alias == chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.CHUNK_LOADED:
                continue
            cb.trigger()

def get_chunk(self) -> ChunkBase | None:
    """Get the owning Chunk if it exists.

    Returns:
        ChunkBase | None: The chunk that owns this object
    """
    if self._chunk_parent is None or self._chunk_parent() is None:
        owner = self.get_owner()
        while owner and not isinstance(owner, ChunkBase):
            owner = owner.get_owner()

        if not owner:
            return None
        self._chunk_parent = weakref.ref(owner)

    return self._chunk_parent()

def get_edit_context(self) -> Sdf.Layer | None:
    """The layer to author this object's stage edits in: its chunk's layer.

    Every param uses the layer of the nearest ChunkBase above it, rather than a layer of its
    own::

        with Usd.EditContext(stage, param.get_edit_context()):
            ...  # modify the stage

    Returns:
        Sdf.Layer | None: The layer, or None when the layer manager is not initialized or
        the layer is muted
    """
    if not chunk_registry.ChunkLayerManager().initialized:
        return

    if c := self.get_chunk():
        layer = chunk_registry.ChunkLayerManager().get_or_create_layer(c)
        # A diff cook running: its scratch layer, which stands in for the chunk's own.
        # Asked for all the same: asking is what places the layer under its Edit Target.
        if (scratch := chunk_cook.cooking_into(c)) is not None:
            return scratch
        if layer and layer.IsMuted():
            return None
        return layer

def get_identifier(self) -> str:
    """A dotted path from the top-most owner to this object, e.g. MyChunk.SomeGroup.MyParam.

    names = [self.name]

        owner = owner.get_owner()
    return ".".join(reversed(names))

def has_flag(self, flag: IntFlag) -> bool:
    """Check if a flag is enabled.

    Args:
        flag (IntFlag): The flag to check

    Returns:
        bool: If the flag is enabled or not
    """
    # Compared as plain ints: IntFlag.__and__ constructs (and caches, and looks up) a
    # whole new flag member just to be thrown away by bool(). This is called millions of
    # times when walking a large graph -- get_chunks() alone asks twice per chunk -- and
    # the enum machinery was measurably the second-largest cost of building one.
    return bool(int(self.flags) & int(flag))

request_delete()

Ask the owners to delete this object; removing their references is their job.

If the object lies within a ChunkContainerBase, the container's remove_param_or_group is called with it. All callbacks are removed from the object and its owner is set to None.

Source code in usd_chunks/chunk_core.py 
def request_delete(self):
    """Ask the owners to delete this object; removing their references is their job.

    If the object lies within a ChunkContainerBase, the container's remove_param_or_group is
    called with it. All callbacks are removed from the object and its owner is set to None.
    """
    # Retire the chunk from module execution before anything is dismantled. Teardown
    # detaches params and edits the layer stack, and both cascade as notices that can
    # re-enter the DAG solve and call this chunk's module.execute() again -- against a
    # half-dismantled chunk whose get_param() now returns None, which is an AttributeError
    # in essentially every chunk script (none of them defend against their own params
    # vanishing mid-run, nor should they have to). Never cleared: a chunk is not reusable
    # after request_delete. Read by chunk_notice's execute dispatch.
    self._deleting = True

    # Make sure we're enabled when deleting as being disabled will block necessary notices from being sent
    self.unset_state(ChunkFlags.State.DISABLED)
    # Same for the 'blocked' flag (set by view-driven re-cook on out-of-view chunks): a blocked
    # chunk suppresses its own notices, so CHUNK_DELETED would never fire and the USD prim would
    # be left behind on the stage.
    self.set_blocked(False)

    if not self.can_delete():
        # Debug, not warning: closing a scene deletes every chunk, so a warning here
        # printed one line per wired chunk each time usdview closed or opened a file.
        logger.debug("Deleting %s, which still has wires out; disconnecting them", self.name)
        self.get_dag_node().disconnect()

    owner = self.get_owner()
    if owner and isinstance(owner, ChunkContainerBase):
        # Owner is a group, so delete this param from the group
        owner.remove_param_or_group(self)
    elif owner and isinstance(owner, NameSyncedContainer):
        # Owner is a NameSyncedContainer, pop it from the container. When successfully removed,
        # the container will send PARAM_REMOVED with it's owning ChunkContainerBase as sender.
        owner.pop(self)

    # Disconnected, not only dropped: a connection sits in a reference cycle, so it lives
    # on until the cyclic GC runs -- and a global one kept hearing every stage meanwhile,
    # the next scene's included, on behalf of a chunk deleted with its own.
    for connection in self._callbacks.get(include_private=True):
        connection.disconnect()
    self._callbacks.clear()
    self.set_owner(None)
    self.send_self(chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.CHUNK_DELETED)

def get_variants(self) -> list:
    """The menu entries, building them first if they were declared lazily.

    Memoised onto the field, so the callable runs once per process however many menus
    are drawn. Callers should use this rather than reading .variants, which may still
    be the callable.

    Returns:
        The variants, empty if building them failed.
    """
    variants = self.variants
    if callable(variants):
        try:
            variants = list(variants())
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a menu must still open
            # Variants are an optional extra on one entry, and this runs while a menu is
            # being drawn for EVERY chunk -- one module that cannot build its list must
            # not take the whole chunk menu with it. Sdr.Registry() can raise, for
            # example, when an installed plugin advertises an invalid version.
            logger.warning("Could not build menu variants for %r: %s", self.module, e)
            return []
        object.__setattr__(self, "variants", variants)
    return variants

def check_hierarchy(self):
    """A debug function for checking the hierarchy structure of a group.

    Raises:
        TypeError: An owner is not set to a child of this group
        TypeError: The owner of a child is not a ChunkNoticePropagator
        ValueError: The owner of a child does not itself hold the child
        NameError: Duplicate chunk in the hierarchy
        NameError: Duplicate name in the hierarchy
    """
    failed_msg = f"check_hierarchy for {self.name} failed! \n"
    failed_msg += " Reason: {}"

    found_params: set[ChunkCommon] = set()

    # Names are checked among siblings, not across the whole hierarchy: a param is
    # addressed relative to its owner, so two groups may each hold a "General"
    # without either becoming unreachable. Renderer settings are the case that
    # proves it -- every installed renderer gets a group and every one of them ends
    # up with a General for its leftovers.
    #
    # Keyed by id() rather than by the owner itself, so this never depends on how a
    # param defines equality: two distinct groups that happen to compare equal must
    # still be two scopes.
    found_names: dict[int, set[str]] = {}

    for p in self.get_params():
        if isinstance(p, ChunkBase):
            # Chunks (inherit from ChunkAttributes) do not need owners
            continue

        owner = p.get_owner()
        if isinstance(owner, NameSyncedContainer):
            # Get the owner of the container, i.e the group or chunk
            owner = owner.get_owner()

        if not owner:
            raise TypeError(
                failed_msg.format(f"{p.name} does not have an owner. All params except Chunks should have an owner")
            )

        if not isinstance(owner, chunk_notice.ChunkNoticePropagator):
            raise TypeError(failed_msg.format(f"{p.name}'s owner is not a ChunkNoticePropagator object"))

        if isinstance(owner, ChunkContainerBase) and not isinstance(owner, ChunkListGroupBase):
            if p not in [x._param_ref if isinstance(x, ProxyParam) else x for x in owner.get_my_params()]:
                raise ValueError(
                    failed_msg.format(f"{p.name} has owner: {owner.name}. Owner does not hold this param")
                )

        if p in found_params:
            raise NameError(failed_msg.format(f"{p.name} is duplicated in the hierarchy"))
        found_params.add(p)

        direct_owner = p.get_owner()
        if isinstance(direct_owner, NameSyncedContainer):
            direct_owner = direct_owner.get_owner()

        siblings = found_names.setdefault(id(direct_owner), set())
        if p.name in siblings:
            owner_name = getattr(direct_owner, "name", "<no owner>")
            raise NameError(
                failed_msg.format(f"param name: {p.name} is not unique under {owner_name}")
            )
        siblings.add(p.name)

        tuple[int, ChunkCommon]: (depth, object), starting with this container
    """
    yield level, self
    for p in self.get_my_params():
        if isinstance(p, ChunkGroupBase):
            yield from p.iter_hierarchy(level + 1)
        else:
            yield level + 1, p

def print_hierarchy(self):
    """Print the container and its children as a tree, for debugging."""

    def inset(i):
        return "." * i * 4

    max_inset = 15

    msg = f"\n{'-' * max_inset}* {self.name} hierarchy *{'-' * max_inset}\n\n"
    for indent, p in self.iter_hierarchy():
        cls_name = f"[{p.__class__.__name__}]"
        if len(cls_name) > max_inset:
            cls_name = f"[{p.__class__.__name__[0 : max_inset - 1]}]"

        offset = "." * (max_inset - len(cls_name))

        msg += f"{cls_name}{offset}{inset(indent)}{p.name}"
        if isinstance(p, ChunkParamBase):
            msg += f" -> {p.evaluate_type().name}"

        owner = p.get_owner()
        if isinstance(owner, NameSyncedContainer):
            # Get the owner of the container, i.e the group or chunk
            owner = owner.get_owner()

        if owner and isinstance(owner, ChunkContainerBase):
            msg += f". Owner = ({owner.name})"

        msg += f". Id = ({hex(id(p))})"
        msg += "\n"

    self.get_logger().info(msg)

def request_delete(self):
    """Delete this container, and with it its children."""
    # Retire from module execution up here, not in the super() call at the end: the child
    # loop below detaches this container's own params, and its PARAM_REMOVED notices can
    # re-enter the DAG solve long before super().request_delete() would set the flag. See
    # ChunkCommon.request_delete for what the flag protects against.
    self._deleting = True

    # Call request_delete on all children. This will send PARAM_REMOVED on the removed
    # children.
    #
    # get_my_params(), not get_params(): the latter walks the whole nested ChainMap, so a
    # context would delete a grandchild param (a sub-chunk's own Menu/Slider) directly,
    # leaving that sub-chunk alive but gutted -- get_param() returning None on a chunk that
    # was never asked to delete, and so never marked _deleting. Anything the teardown then
    # cascades into (reconcile_edit_targets re-running an Edit Target, a refresh callback)
    # crashes on the missing param. Deleting only direct children keeps the order right:
    # each child container tears down its own subtree, marking itself first.
    for param in self.get_my_params():
        param.request_delete()

    self.children.clear()
    self.children.set_owner(None)

    super().request_delete()

def __init__(self, group: GroupT, *args, **kwargs):
    super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

    # Hold a weakref to the group. If all other references to the group is killed, then
    # remove it from the UI as well, as the ui should not take ownership of the group
    self._group = weakref.ref(group, self._group_deleted)

    self._callbacks: list[chunk_notice.NoticeConnection] = []

    # Add a parameter to this widget whenever a param was added to the group
    self._callbacks.append(
        chunk_notice.NoticeConnection(
            self._param_added_callback, chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.PARAM_ADDED, self.group
        )
    )

    # Remove a parameter when the parameter was removed from the group
    self._callbacks.append(
        chunk_notice.NoticeConnection(
            self._param_removed_callback, chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.PARAM_REMOVED, self.group
        )
    )

    # Calls _delete_self() whenever the chunk sends the CHUNK_DELETED
    self._callbacks.append(
        chunk_notice.NoticeConnection(self._delete_self, chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.CHUNK_DELETED, self.group)
    )

    # Listen to state changes on the group
    self._callbacks.append(
        chunk_notice.NoticeConnection(
            self._state_changed,
            chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.STATE_CHANGED,
            self.group.get_attribute_sender("state"),
        )
    )

    self._callbacks.append(
        chunk_notice.NoticeConnection(
            self._name_changed,
            chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.ATTRIBUTE_CHANGED,
            self.group.get_attribute_sender("name"),
        )
    )

    self._callbacks.append(
        chunk_notice.NoticeConnection(
            self._name_changed,
            chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.ATTRIBUTE_CHANGED,
            self.group.get_attribute_sender("label"),
        )
    )

    self._callbacks.append(
        chunk_notice.NoticeConnection(
            self._layout_changed,
            chunk_notice.ChunkNoticeAlias.ATTRIBUTE_CHANGED,
            self.group.get_attribute_sender("layout"),
        )
    )

    # Associate ChunkParamGroup objects with group widgets
    self.group_widgets: weakref.WeakValueDictionary[ChunkHash, ChunkContainerWidgetBase] = (
        weakref.WeakValueDictionary()
    )

    # Container for all widgets in this chunk. Dict will map between ChunkParam -> widget
    # for each widget created from the same ChunkParam instance
    self.param_widgets: weakref.WeakValueDictionary[ChunkHash, ChunkParamWidgetBase] = weakref.WeakValueDictionary()

    # Initialize everything
    self.factory = self.get_widget_factory()
    self.build_collapsable()
    self._children_built = not (
        self.defer_collapsed_children
        and self.group.has_flag(ChunkFlags.GroupFlags.COLLAPSABLE)
        and self.group.has_state(ChunkFlags.State.COLLAPSED)
    )
    if self._children_built:
        self._build_param_widgets(self.group)
    self.update_from_layout()
    self.update_from_flags()
    self.update_from_state()

@abstractmethod
def update_from_state(self):
    """Apply the group's HIDDEN, DISABLED and SELECTED state to the widget.

    A group is disabled only by its own DISABLED state. ParamFlags.OUTPUT means nothing for a
    group, and it shares a bit with GroupFlags.COLLAPSABLE, so testing it here would disable
    every collapsible group's children.
    """
    self.set_hidden(self.group.has_state(ChunkFlags.State.HIDDEN))
    # NB: OUTPUT is a ParamFlags value and has no meaning for a group. Checking it
    # here against the group's GroupFlags mis-fires because ParamFlags.OUTPUT and
    # GroupFlags.COLLAPSABLE share the same bit (2), so every collapsible group
    # read as "output" and disabled all its children. A group is only disabled by
    # its own DISABLED state.
    self.set_enabled(not self.group.has_state(ChunkFlags.State.DISABLED))
    self.set_selected(self.group.has_state(ChunkFlags.State.SELECTED))

def add_param(self, param: ChunkT, force_unique: bool = True) -> ChunkT:
    """Add a param to this group's children.

    Changes to the param propagate to this group, since they share the same hierarchy; see
    ChunkNoticePropagator. To add the same param several times, add clones::

        group.add_param(param.clone())
        group.add_params([param, param.clone(), param.clone()])

    Args:
        param (ChunkT): A parameter to add. May also be another ChunkContainer, which will nest the group
        force_unique (bool): If a param already exists in the hierarchy, we most often do not want a direct duplicate.
            This enables the check, and if a duplicate exists, raises a ValueError. However, if the hash is unique but
            the name is a duplicate, this will resolve the name conflict by incrementing a numerical suffix. If set to False,
            this check is never performed, instead any duplicate will simply replace the old parameter. Defaults to True

    Returns:
        ChunkT: The param

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the param is a direct duplicate (hash exists already)
    """
    new_param = None
    if force_unique:
        new_param = self.resolve_new_param(param)

    if new_param is None or new_param is param:
        new_param = param

    if isinstance(new_param, ChunkCommon):
        # Add the new param to self.children container. The owner/ownee relationship is handled
        # by the container, so should not modify owner here
        self.children.add(new_param)

        if isinstance(new_param, ChunkContainerBase):
            # Also append the children of the group, as this allows for fast lookups across the layers
            self.children.add_nested(new_param.children)

    else:
        raise ValueError("Chunks only support params inherited from ChunkCommon")
    return new_param

def add_params(self, params: Iterable[ChunkT], force_unique: bool = True, clone: bool = False) -> list[ChunkT]:
    """Add several params, calling add_param on each.

    Args:
        params (Iterable[ChunkCommon]): The chunk objects to add
        force_unique (bool, optional): Force unique param names. Defaults to True.
        clone (bool, optional): Add clones instead of the params themselves. Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        list[ChunkCommon]: The added params, which differ from the input if clones were made
    """
    new_params = []
    for param in params:
        if clone:
            p = self.add_param(param.clone(), force_unique)
        else:
            p = self.add_param(param, force_unique)
        new_params.append(p)
    return new_params

def resolve_new_param(self, param: ChunkT) -> ChunkT | None:
    """The param, renamed if its name conflicts with another child of this group.

    Args:
        param (ChunkParamBase): A param or container

    Returns:
        ChunkT: The param, possibly with a new name

    Raises:
        ValueError: The same param (same hash) is already here
    """
    # A key lookup down the ChainMap, not `param in self.get_params()`: that materialised
    # every param of every nested container (a tuple of ChainMap.values(), each entry a
    # walk of the chain) to answer a membership question, on every add. On a context it
    # is the whole scene, so appending the 50th chunk to a chain cost 5x the first --
    # the one thing about a node graph that must not get slower as the graph grows.
    if param in self.children:
        raise ValueError(f"A duplicate for param {param.name} was found on container {self.name}")

    new_param = param

    if not isinstance(param, ProxyParam):
        reserved_names = self.get_reserved_names()

        new_name = self.get_valid_child_name(param.name, reserved_names)
        new_param.name = new_name

        reserved_names.add(new_name)

        # A chunk entering a scene or chunkgroup keeps its own param names: they are
        # attrs on its own prim, so they can't clash with another chunk. Renamed, a
        # group called "Output" became "Output1" next to a chunk named Output, and its
        # saved values were not read back on reopen.
        entering_context = isinstance(new_param, ChunkBase) and self.has_flag(ChunkFlags.GroupFlags.CONTEXT)
        if isinstance(new_param, ChunkGroupBase) and not entering_context:
            for p in new_param.get_params():
                if not isinstance(p, ProxyParam):
                    new_name = self.get_valid_child_name(p.name, reserved_names)
                    reserved_names.add(new_name)
                    p.name = new_name

    return new_param

def get_indexed_param(
    self, param: ChunkCommon | str | HashVal, index: int, predicate: Predicate[ValueT] | None = None
) -> ChunkCommon | None | ValueT:
    """The proxy of a param in one row.

    Args:
        param (ChunkCommon | str | HashVal): The param to look for, or its name
        index (int): The row, an index into proxy_params
        predicate (Predicate[ValueT] | None): Only return the proxy if it matches this. Defaults to None

    Returns:
        ChunkCommon | None: The proxy of param in that row

    Raises:
        IndexError: If the index is out of bounds
    """
    if len(self.proxy_params) == 0 and not predicate:
        return

    if index >= len(self.proxy_params):
        raise IndexError("Index out of range")

    res = self.proxy_params[index].get_param(param)
    if not predicate or predicate(res):
        return res

    raise ValueError(f"Predicate {predicate} failed for get_indexed_param with index {index}")

def remove_index(self, index: int):
    """Remove one row, reducing the size by 1.

    The row's group gets request_delete(). An index out of range is logged and ignored.

    Args:
        index (int): The row to remove
    """
    try:
        self.proxy_params[index].get_dag_node().disconnect()
        self._delete_row(index)
    except IndexError as e:
        self.get_logger().warning("Failed to remove index from list. Index out of range %s", e)
        return

    self.size -= 1
    self._renumber_row_refs([index])

Add a DagNode input; refused across a chunk boundary.

A param-level dependency is in-memory only: ChunkStageSync._on_dependency_added authors inputs:chunk for ChunkBase pairs and returns early for anything else, so an edge between two params is never written to USD, draws no wire in the node graph, and is gone after a reload. Within one chunk that is exactly right -- this is the dirty/ordering edge behind set_function, and it can drive attributes (menu_items, a label, visibility) that no expression can reach. Across two chunks it is a connection nobody can see, and the solve no longer tells a chunk what reaches it across one (chunk_notice: chunks speak only through wires), so it would not even update. An expression is the wire that persists; connect_value redirects to one.

def add_dependency(self, input: chunk_notice.ChunkNoticePropagator) -> int:
    """Add a DagNode input; refused across a chunk boundary.

    A param-level dependency is in-memory only: ChunkStageSync._on_dependency_added
    authors inputs:chunk for ChunkBase pairs and returns early for anything else, so
    an edge between two params is never written to USD, draws no wire in the node
    graph, and is gone after a reload. Within one chunk that is exactly right -- this
    is the dirty/ordering edge behind set_function, and it can drive attributes
    (menu_items, a label, visibility) that no expression can reach. Across two chunks
    it is a connection nobody can see, and the solve no longer tells a chunk what
    reaches it across one (chunk_notice: chunks speak only through wires), so it would
    not even update. An expression is the wire that persists; connect_value redirects
    to one.

    Args:
        input: The propagator to depend on.

    Returns:
        The dependency index.

    Raises:
        ValueError: input is a param of another chunk.
    """
    if isinstance(input, ChunkParamBase) and (pair := self._cross_chunk_ref(input)):
        mine, theirs = pair
        ref = self._expression_ref_to(input, theirs) or f"@{theirs.name}.<param>@"
        raise ValueError(
            f"Param dependency {mine.name}.{self.name} <- {theirs.name}.{input.name} crosses "
            f"chunks: chunks connect only through wires. Use an expression instead: "
            f"{mine.name}.{self.name} = \"{ref}\" (or connect_value, which authors one)"
        )
    return super().add_dependency(input)

def connect_value(self, other: ChunkParamBase[ValueT]):
    """Make this param's value follow another param's.

    Across chunks this authors an expression instead of a DagNode edge, since an expression
    is written to USD, draws a wire and survives a reload.

    Args:
        other: The param to follow.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The two params' types are not compatible, or other is in another
            chunk and no @Node.param@ reaches it -- its name resolves to a different
            param of that chunk.
    """
    my_t = self.evaluate_type()
    other_t = other.evaluate_type()
    if my_t not in other_t:
        raise ValueError(f"Can't connect {other_t.name} to parameter {my_t}")

    # Across chunks, do what the caller asked for in the form that survives: an
    # expression authors the USD connection, draws the wire, and is patched on rename,
    # where the DagNode edge below would quietly vanish on the next load. The type
    # check above still ran, which the raw expression path skips.
    if pair := self._cross_chunk_ref(other):
        ref = self._expression_ref_to(other, pair[1])
        if ref is None:
            # Chunks connect only through wires, and an expression is the only wire a
            # param can have to another chunk's.
            raise ValueError(
                f"Can't connect {pair[0].name}.{self.name} to {pair[1].name}.{other.name}: "
                f"no @{pair[1].name}.<param>@ reaches it, as its name resolves to another "
                "param of that chunk. Give it a name of its own."
            )
        logger.debug(
            "connect_value across chunks (%s -> %s): authoring %s",
            pair[1].name, pair[0].name, ref,
        )
        self.value = ref
        return

    idx = -1
    # If other already is connected to self, then we can use that index
    for i, node in self.get_dependencies(is_inst(type(other))):
        if node == other:
            idx = i
            break

    if idx == -1:
        # The nodes are not connected, so we add other as dependency
        idx = self.add_dependency(other)
    self.set_function("value", lambda x, _: x.get_dependency(idx, is_inst(type(other))).value)
